uncertainties: Video links were found on YouTube search-result pages and each one was checked with YouTube's oEmbed API (title + channel) on 2026-10-01. Durations and view counts come from the search results and are approximate.
phy-dual-nature, phy-atoms and phy-nuclei share one JEE Wallah 'Modern Physics' one-shot (10h 42m) that covers all three; there is no separate verified PW one-shot for each.
phy-kinetic-theory uses a combined JEE Wallah 'KTG & Thermodynamics' one-shot.

Eduniti (Mohit Goenka) videos are short revision/formula videos (10–60 min), not full lectures; several chapters are split across parts (Rotational Motion, Fluids, Waves, Wave Optics, Modern Physics) and only one part is linked.
phy-experimental-physics: no single PW one-shot for the 'Experimental Skills' unit was found; linked videos are an Eduniti question-practice video and a Vedantu JEE English lecture (from 2024).
phy-magnetism-matter: the PW video is a 60-minute revision, not a full lecture.
phy-semiconductors: the Eduniti video covers only logic gates.
Video language: JEE Wallah, Eduniti and Vedantu JEE Made Ejee are marked hinglish (Hindi with English terms). This is a general judgement, not checked video by video.

Notes pages (Aakash, Vedantu) were fetched and confirmed to load with a matching title. Aakash has no separate Thermodynamics, Atoms or Nuclei page, so Vedantu revision notes are linked for those. phy-center-of-mass uses the Aakash Rotational Motion sheet, whose Centre of Mass section does not cover collisions.

Book chapter numbers are given only for HC Verma (fixed numbering). DC Pandey and Cengage chapter numbers change between editions, so only the volume and chapter name are given; names may differ slightly by edition. Irodov section names are from the standard edition; Irodov is optional and only for Advanced.

ncert_useful is a judgement call: true where JEE Main often asks NCERT-style theory or fact questions (modern physics, semiconductors, EM waves, magnetism and matter, optics, thermal physics, units, experiments). False where NCERT exercises are too easy to help with JEE problem-solving, though NCERT theory should still be read.
